items.title: Trump May Not Be Entirely Wrong About A.I.
items.author: Bret Stephens
items.content: <article>Has A.I. become death, destroyer of worlds?</article>

items.title: Scrutiny of Jury May Complicate Future of Lindsay Clancy Case
items.author: Jenna Russell and Nicholas Bogel-Burroughs
items.content: <article>The intense public focus on the jurors whose deadlock led to a mistrial could complicate any attempt to retry the case, and to seat jurors in other high-profile cases.</article>

items.title: Kennedy Center Closes Its Doors Despite a Judge’s Order
items.author: Julia Jacobs and Zach Montague
items.content: <article>The announcement came after President Trump said he would cancel a $257 million renovation of the venue if his name is not returned to the building.</article>

items.title: It’s Already Too Late to Stop the A.I. Threat
items.author: Thomas L. Friedman
items.content: <article>China and the United States must work to repair the damage A.I. has done now, not look to future developments.</article>

items.title: Trump Threatens to Cancel Kennedy Center Renovation
items.author: Matthew Cullen
items.content: <article>Also, the world is furious over rising prices. Here’s the latest at the end of Tuesday.</article>

items.title: A T. Rex Walked Here: Teacher Finds Rare Footprints in North Dakota
items.author: Adeel Hassan
items.content: <article>Kent Hups, a high school science teacher in Colorado, discovered a 23-foot trackway of fossilized dinosaur footprints, which offer a glimpse of how the apex predator moved 66 million years ago.</article>

items.title: Rising Fuel Prices Set Off Anger and Protests Around the World
items.author: Damien Cave
items.content: <article>From Indonesia to Guatemala to Syria, shortages and price increases are leading to protests and blackouts.</article>

items.title: Jamie Beaton Could Be the World’s Most Educated Person
items.author: Scott Cacciola
items.content: <article>Jamie Beaton has 12 advanced degrees from Harvard, Yale, Oxford and other top universities, with more on the way. Why? How?</article>

items.title: Do You Have Questions About A.I.? We Want to Answer Them.
items.author: Cade Metz
items.content: <article>The New York Times is soliciting readers’ questions about the dangers — and benefits — posed by artificial intelligence.</article>
